mainTopic: Teaching Torah in public, how long a נזיפה lasts, and דרשות on the last words of דוד
overview: This amud finishes רבי's דרשה that Torah should be learned in private. It then tells how רבי חייא taught רב and רבה בר בר חנה in the marketplace, upset רבי, and kept a נזיפה on himself for thirty days. The גמרא explains רבי's two messages on day thirty through the question of מקצת היום ככולו. It then gives the two sides: רבי reads 'חכמות בחוץ תרונה' like רבא, while רבי חייא applies ״חמוקי ירכיך״ to צדקה and גמילות חסדים. The thirty days are explained as special to a נשיא, and three stories show that a נזיפה in בבל lasts one day. The last story leads to the 'last words of דוד', ה׳'s rebuke of דוד for singing over שאול, and the reading of 'כושי' as someone who stands out in his deeds. Then come דרשות on דוד's 'mighty men' as praises of his humility, power and strength, along with his sin with אוריה. The amud ends by naming who said a new teaching about the laws of נידוי, which comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Torah should be taught in private
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי's דרשה: just as the thigh is hidden, so too דברי תורה should be kept private.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, words of Torah are to be kept hidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a comparison it started earlier: Torah learning should be done in private, not out in the open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes the דרשה behind רבי's rule against teaching students in the marketplace. It is the rule that the next story is about, because רבי חייא will go and teach in the market anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the background for the whole story that follows.

phrases.english: So too, words of Torah are in private.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the דרשה begun before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Torah should be taught in private and not in the marketplace.

steps.title: רבי חייא teaches his nephews in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught רב and רבה בר בר חנה in the market. רבי heard about it and was upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא went out and taught his two nephews, רב and רבה בר בר חנה, in the marketplace. רבי heard and became upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story where רבי חייא does exactly what רבי's rule said not to do: he teaches Torah in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the rule being broken by a great sage, which sets up a conflict with רבי. רבי's anger is the starting point for everything that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Became upset, was strict about it

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya went out and taught
his two nephews in the marketplace,
Rav and Rabbah bar bar Chana.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the second "bar" (in round brackets) and some don't.

phrases.english: Rebbi heard, and became upset.
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story about someone going against the rule just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא taught in public against רבי's rule, and רבי was upset.

steps.title: רבי hints that רבי חייא should leave
steps.stepSummary: When רבי חייא came to visit, רבי said to him: "עייא, who is calling you outside?"
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא came to visit him. רבי said to him: עייא, who is calling you outside?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא visits רבי, and רבי answers with a sharp hint showing he is upset about the teaching outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not scold him openly. The words "calling you outside" echo where רבי חייא taught, in public, and hint that he should step out.

keyTerms.meaning: To visit him (literally, to be seen by him)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya came to visit him,
he said to him: Iyya,
who is calling you outside!
phrases.notes: A hint: since you went outside to teach, go back outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי's anger came out when they met.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי showed his displeasure with a pointed remark.

steps.title: רבי חייא treats himself as rebuked for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא understood that רבי was hurt, so he took on himself the status of נזיפה for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He understood that רבי had taken the matter to heart, so he conducted himself as rebuked for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא reads the hint correctly and, on his own, acts as someone who was formally rebuked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזיפה is a kind of rebuke where the person keeps his distance in shame. The thirty-day length matters later: in step 20 the גמרא tries to learn from it how long a נזיפה lasts, and in step 21 it explains that a rebuke from the נשיא, which רבי was, is different.

phrases.english: He knew that he had taken the matter to heart,
he kept the status of rebuke on himself
for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי חייא's reaction to רבי's remark.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא took a thirty-day נזיפה on himself.

steps.title: רבי invites him on day thirty, then cancels
steps.stepSummary: On the thirtieth day רבי sent word, "Come." Then he sent word again that he should not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the thirtieth day he sent to him: Come. Then he sent again that he should not come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי changes his mind on the last day, first inviting רבי חייא and then telling him to wait. This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the story itself explains why רבי changed his mind. That gap is exactly what the גמרא will ask about next.

phrases.english: On the thirtieth day he sent to him: Come.
Then he sent to him again that he should not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The end of the thirty days, with two opposite messages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי first ended the נזיפה on day thirty, then held off.

steps.title: Why did רבי change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי was thinking at first and what he was thinking in the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, what did he hold? And in the end, what did he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to ask what reasoning stood behind each of רבי's two messages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes רבי had a real halachic reason both times, not just a change of mood. It turns the story into a question about counting days.

phrases.english: At first, what did he hold
and in the end, what did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי סְבַר וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי סְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two messages in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic reasoning behind רבי's first and second messages.

steps.title: Does part of a day count as the whole day?
steps.stepSummary: At first רבי held מקצת היום ככולו, so the thirtieth day had already counted. In the end he held we do not say that here.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he held: part of the day is like the whole day. In the end he held: we do not say part of the day is like the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי's change of mind was about one rule: whether part of the thirtieth day counts as a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מקצת היום ככולו applies, once day thirty begins the thirty days are done, so רבי said "Come." When he decided the rule does not apply here, the full thirtieth day still had to pass, so he told רבי חייא not to come yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the day counts like the whole day

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's two messages reflect two views on מקצת היום ככולו. In the end he held that the rule does not apply to this נזיפה, so the full thirty days were needed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי did not deny that רבי חייא's thirty days were nearly over. The only question was whether the thirtieth day counts once it starts, or only once it is fully over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to the wider question of when a partial day counts in halachic time periods, such as the days of mourning.

phrases.english: At first he held:
part of the day is like the whole of it.
And in the end he held:
we do not say part of the day is like the whole of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At first רבי held מקצת היום ככולו and so ended the נזיפה on day thirty. In the end he held the rule does not apply, so the whole thirtieth day was needed.

steps.title: רבי חייא arrives, and רבי asks why he came
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא comes on the thirtieth day. רבי asks why, and רבי חייא says it is because רבי sent for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end רבי חייא came. רבי asked him: Why did you come? He answered: Because you, my master, sent me word to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רבי חייא shows up, and רבי asks him why he came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי sent two messages: first 'come,' then 'don't come.' רבי חייא's answer shows he is acting on the first message only.

keyTerms.meaning: Master (a polite way to address a teacher)

phrases.english: In the end he came.
He said to him: Why have you come?
phrases.notes: רבי is the one asking, and רבי חייא is the one who came.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּשָׁלַח לִי מָר דְּלֵיתֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because the master sent me word that I should come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the גמרא explained why רבי changed his mind in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא came because he received רבי's first message.

steps.title: רבי objects that he also sent a second message
steps.stepSummary: רבי points out that he also sent a message telling רבי חייא not to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I sent you word that you should not come!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back. He reminds רבי חייא about the second message, which said not to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חייא knew about both messages, coming would mean ignoring the later one. The challenge is: why did you follow the first message and not the second?

phrases.english: But I sent you word that you should not come!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חייא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was a later message cancelling the first one, so coming seems wrong.

steps.title: רבי חייא never saw the second messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that he saw the first messenger but not the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one I saw, and that one I did not see.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers the challenge. The second message never reached him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was not ignoring רבי. He only knew about the 'come' message, so he came on the thirtieth day and was released from the נזיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A formal rebuke; the person keeps a distance for a set time

phrases.english: He said to him: This one I saw,
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the first messenger, who said to come.

phrases.english: and that one I did not see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's objection in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: the second message never arrived.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא ignored the second message.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never received it, so he acted correctly.

steps.title: רבי sees Heaven's help and quotes a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי applies a פסוק from משלי to רבי חייא: when ה׳ is pleased with a person, He makes peace for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read this verse about him: 'When ה׳ is pleased with a man's ways, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ends the episode. He sees that the second message missing רבי חייא was a sign from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי understands that ה׳ arranged things so that רבי חייא would be released from his נזיפה and peace would be restored. רבי חייא did nothing wrong, and Heaven helped him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא came only because the second message never reached him, and רבי saw this as Heaven's help.

phrases.english: He read about him:
"When ה׳ is pleased with a man's ways,
phrases.notes: משלי 16:7

phrases.english: He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי reacts to רבי חייא's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Heaven helped רבי חייא, and the rift between them was healed.

steps.title: רבי asks why רבי חייא acted as he did
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks רבי חייא for his reason for what he did earlier, which started the whole story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did you, master, act this way?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that peace is restored, רבי asks רבי חייא to explain his original action. This sets up the discussion of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes back to the start of the story, when רבי חייא taught Torah out in the open even though רבי had told him not to. רבי wants to hear his reasoning.

phrases.english: What is the reason the master acted this way?
phrases.notes: He means רבי חייא's teaching Torah in the marketplace, which began the whole story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story is resolved, returns to the original cause of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי חייא's source for teaching in public.

steps.title: רבי חייא quotes 'חכמות בחוץ תרונה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says he taught outside because of the פסוק, 'Wisdom cries aloud in the streets.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is written: 'Wisdom cries aloud in the streets.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives his source, a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק simply: Torah (wisdom) should be called out in the streets. So teaching in public is what the פסוק asks for.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
"Wisdom cries aloud in the streets."
phrases.notes: משלי 1:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'חכמות בחוץ תרונה' tells us to teach Torah in public.

steps.title: רבי says רבי חייא did not understand the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that רבי חייא did not study the פסוק deeply enough or was not taught its real meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you read it once, you did not read it a second time. If you read it a second time, you did not read it a third time. And if you read it a third time, they did not explain it to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rejects רבי חייא's reading of the פסוק. He says the simple reading is not the true meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is not saying the פסוק is unimportant. He is saying רבי חייא took it too simply. The real meaning will be given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You went over it a second time
You went over it a third time

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם קָרִיתָ — לֹא שָׁנִיתָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: If you read it, you did not review it a second time,
and if you reviewed it a second time, you did not review it a third time,
and if you reviewed it a third time, they did not explain it to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי חייא's simple reading of 'חכמות בחוץ תרונה'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain reading misses the פסוק's true meaning.

steps.title: The real meaning of the פסוק, according to רבא
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that one who learns Torah in private will have his Torah announce his greatness in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Wisdom cries aloud in the streets' follows רבא, who said: Whoever learns Torah inside, his Torah announces him outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי understood the פסוק, using רבא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'outside' in the פסוק is not where the learning happens. The learning is done privately, and the result, a person's greatness in Torah, becomes known outside. So the פסוק does not support teaching in the street.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy learning Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Learning in private makes a person's Torah known in public. That is how רבי reads 'חכמות בחוץ תרונה'.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בחוץ' as the place to learn. In רבא's reading, 'outside' is where the Torah's fame spreads, not where the learning happens.

phrases.english: "Wisdom cries aloud in the streets" is like רבא's teaching.
As רבא said:
Whoever is busy with Torah inside,
his Torah announces him outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct explanation that step 14 said רבי חייא was missing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Private Torah learning leads to public recognition. The פסוק is not a command to teach in the street.

steps.title: Challenge from a פסוק in ישעיה about speaking openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a פסוק that says ה׳ did not speak in secret, which suggests Torah should be taught openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'From the beginning I did not speak in secret'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רבי's view, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah is meant for private learning, why does this פסוק stress that it was not said in secret? This seems to support teaching in public, like רבי חייא.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"From the beginning I have not spoken in secret"!
phrases.notes: ישעיה 48:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the private-learning reading in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that Torah should be learned privately, not taught in public
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says Torah was not spoken in secret, which suggests open, public teaching.

steps.title: That פסוק is about the days of the כלה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about not speaking in secret refers to the days of the כלה, the big public Torah gatherings.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק refers to the days of the כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Public teaching fits a special time, not every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the כלה gatherings, many people come to hear Torah, so teaching openly is right then. At other times, the rule from רבא stays in place: learn in private. Both פסוקים are true, each at its own time.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of the כלה, times of large public Torah gatherings

steps.whatToRemember: Normally Torah is learned in private. Public teaching fits the days of the כלה.

phrases.english: That is referring to the days of the כלה.
phrases.notes: The כלה was a time when crowds gathered to hear Torah taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenging פסוק to a specific time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means Torah should always be taught in public.
steps.terutzMaskana: Public teaching is for the days of the כלה. Otherwise private learning is the rule.

steps.title: How does רבי חייא explain the פסוק about hidden thighs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי חייא understands the פסוק ״חמוקי ירכיך״, which seems to say Torah should be kept hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא, what does he do with this פסוק, ״Your rounded thighs״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חייא explains a פסוק that seems to go against his practice of teaching in public. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ״חמוקי ירכיך״ was used to show that Torah should be learned in a hidden, private way. רבי חייא taught in the open, so he must read this פסוק differently. The גמרא wants to know how.

keyTerms.meaning: Your rounded thighs (a פסוק in שיר השירים about hidden things)
What does he do with it? (How does he explain this source?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya,
this verse, "Your rounded thighs"
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:2

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of רבי's view is finished, the גמרא turns to ask how רבי חייא deals with the פסוק that supports רבי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי חייא explains ״חמוקי ירכיך״ without accepting that Torah must be hidden.

steps.title: רבי חייא applies the פסוק to צדקה and גמילות חסדים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says the פסוק is about צדקה and גמילות חסדים, which should be done privately. It is not about Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He applies it to צדקה and to גמילות חסדים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא reads the פסוק as being about charity and acts of kindness, not about Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things like צדקה should be done quietly and in private. So ״hidden like thighs״ fits them well. That leaves רבי חייא free to say Torah should be taught in public.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it up as being about (he applies the פסוק to)

phrases.english: He applies it
to charity and to acts of kindness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא reads ״חמוקי ירכיך״ as being about private צדקה and גמילות חסדים, not Torah study.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי says Torah should be learned privately, based on ״חמוקי ירכיך״. רבי חייא says that פסוק is about doing צדקה and חסד quietly, so Torah may be taught in public.

steps.title: The story seems to show a נזיפה in ארץ ישראל lasts thirty days
steps.stepSummary: From the story, where רבי חייא kept himself rebuked for thirty days, the גמרא learns that a נזיפה in ארץ ישראל lasts thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that their rebuke (in ארץ ישראל) lasts thirty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a rule from the story. רבי חייא stayed under a rebuke for thirty days, so it seems a rebuke in ארץ ישראל lasts that long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns from the story about teaching Torah to a halachic question: how long does a נזיפה last? The story looks like proof that in ארץ ישראל it is thirty days. That is longer than the shorter time mentioned before.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems / this shows that
A rebuke, a lighter form of shunning than נידוי

phrases.english: So it seems their rebuke
phrases.notes: This looks back at the story: רבי חייא kept himself rebuked by רבי for thirty days.

phrases.english: lasts thirty days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of public Torah teaching and draws a halachic rule about נזיפה from the same story.
steps.raayaObject: How long a נזיפה lasts in ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא kept himself rebuked for thirty days after רבי's rebuke.

steps.title: A rebuke from the נשיא is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the proof: רבי was the נשיא, and a rebuke from the נשיא is more serious.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rebuke from the נשיא is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from step 20. The thirty days came from a rebuke by the נשיא, which is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי was the נשיא, his rebuke carried extra weight and lasted longer. So the story does not set the rule for an ordinary rebuke in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the Sanhedrin (here, רבי)

phrases.english: The rebuke of the Nasi is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back the proof drawn in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the story as a general rule. It does not deny that רבי חייא was rebuked for thirty days.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story is about a rebuke from the נשיא, a special case that cannot be used for ordinary rebukes.

steps.title: How long does a נזיפה last in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a נזיפה lasts in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our rebuke (in בבל), how long is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about rebukes among the Sages of בבל. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After talking about rebukes in ארץ ישראל, the גמרא asks the same thing about its own community.

phrases.english: And our rebuke, how long is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rebukes in ארץ ישראל to rebukes in בבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long a נזיפה lasts in בבל.

steps.title: In בבל, one day
steps.stepSummary: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a rebuke in בבל lasts only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the rule. The story that comes next serves as its proof.

phrases.english: One day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.

steps.title: Background: how שמואל and מר עוקבא honored each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its proof with a story. It first describes how שמואל and מר עוקבא each gave the other honor in a different setting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the story of שמואל and מר עוקבא. When they sat and learned, מר עוקבא sat in front of שמואל, four אמות away. When they sat in judgment, שמואל sat in front of מר עוקבא, four אמות away. They would lower a spot in the mat for מר עוקבא, and he sat on it so that שמואל's words could be heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story that proves the ״one day״ rule. This part only sets the scene, showing how the two great men respected each other. The actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Torah learning, שמואל was greater, so מר עוקבא treated him like his teacher. In court, מר עוקבא was the head judge, so שמואל gave him honor. Even in court, מר עוקבא sat lower so that שמואל's Torah would be heard clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות (about 2 meters), a distance of respect

phrases.english: As in the case of Shmuel and Mar Ukva,
when they would sit and study halacha,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב מָר עוּקְבָא קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: Mar Ukva would sit before Shmuel
at a distance of four cubits.
And when they would sit in judgment,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יָתֵיב שְׁמוּאֵל קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר עוּקְבָא
phrases.english: Shmuel would sit before Mar Ukva
at a distance of four cubits.
And they would lower a place
for Mar Ukva in the mat,
and he would sit on it
so that his words would be heard.
phrases.notes: "His words" here means שמואל's Torah, so it could be heard even while they were judging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that proves the answer of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That a נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שמואל and מר עוקבא (this step sets the scene).

steps.title: מר עוקבא rebukes himself for one day
steps.stepSummary: One day מר עוקבא was distracted and let שמואל walk him home. When he saw שמואל was hurt, he kept himself under a נזיפה for one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day מר עוקבא walked שמואל to his lodging. One day he was busy thinking about a court case, and שמואל walked behind him. When they reached מר עוקבא's house, שמואל said: Isn't this enough for you? Release me, sir, from this duty! מר עוקבא realized שמואל was upset, so he kept himself under a נזיפה for one day.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the story and gives the proof. מר עוקבא kept himself under a rebuke for exactly one day, which shows that a נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally מר עוקבא honored שמואל as his teacher by walking him home. When the roles got reversed by mistake, שמואל's sharp words showed he was hurt. מר עוקבא kept himself rebuked for one day, and that length matches the rule in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Walks someone home to honor them
Took the matter to heart (was hurt)

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day, as we see from מר עוקבא. The thirty days of רבי חייא was a special case because a rebuke from the נשיא is more serious.

phrases.english: Every day would accompany
Mar Ukva Shmuel until his lodging.
One day he was preoccupied with his case,
and Shmuel was walking behind him.
When he reached his house,
he said to him: Is it not enough for you?
phrases.notes: שמואל is the one speaking, after walking מר עוקבא all the way home.

phrases.english: Let the master release me from my obligation!
He knew that he had taken the matter to heart,
so he conducted himself as rebuked for one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story started in step 24 and gives the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מר עוקבא kept himself rebuked for one day after upsetting שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נזיפה among the Sages of בבל lasts one day.

steps.title: The woman who did not move her leg
steps.stepSummary: A woman did not move aside for a תלמיד חכם, and he called her rude. רב נחמן told her to keep a נזיפה for one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman was sitting on a path with her leg stretched out, sifting barley. A young Torah scholar passed by, and she did not pull her leg in for him. He said, 'How rude that woman is!' She came to רב נחמן. He asked, 'Did you hear him say the word שמתא (ban)?' She said no. He said, 'Then go and keep a rebuke on yourself for one day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story to prove that a נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling her 'rude' was not a full ban (שמתא), since he never said that word. So רב נחמן treats it as a נזיפה, and he tells her to keep it for exactly one day. This backs up the answer in Step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: A full ban (נידוי), which is stronger than a rebuke
A rebuke (נזיפה), a lighter kind of shunning

phrases.english: A certain woman was sitting on a path,
she had her leg stretched out
and she was sifting barley.
A young Torah scholar was passing by
and she did not move aside for him.
He said: How rude that woman is!
She came before רב נחמן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: מִי שְׁמַעְתְּ שַׁמְתָּא מִפּוּמֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: He said to her: Did you hear the word 'ban' from his mouth?
She said to him: No.
He said to her: Go, keep a rebuke
on yourself for one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story supporting the one-day length of a נזיפה in בבל.
steps.raayaObject: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling to the woman: keep a נזיפה for one day.

steps.title: זוטרא בר טוביה asks about the 'last words' of דוד
steps.stepSummary: While reading before רב יהודה, זוטרא בר טוביה asked: if the פסוק says 'last words,' what were the first words?
steps.simpleTranslation: זוטרא בר טוביה was reading a section of the נביא before רב יהודה. When he reached the פסוק 'Now these are the last words of דוד,' he said: 'Last' means there were also first words. What are the first words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third story that will also prove the one-day נזיפה. This step is the setup: a student asks his רבי a hard question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'last' (אחרונים) suggests there were earlier 'words' of דוד, but it is not clear where they are. This question sets up the awkward moment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Reading through a section of פסוקים

phrases.aramaic: זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה הֲוָה קָפָסֵיק סִידְרָא
phrases.english: זוטרא בר טוביה was reading a section
before רב יהודה.
When he reached this verse:
"Now these are the last words of David,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:1

phrases.english: he said to him: "Last"
implies that there are first ones.
What are the first ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה הֲוָה קָפָסֵיק סִידְרָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that will also support the one-day נזיפה.
steps.raayaObject: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of זוטרא בר טוביה and רב יהודה (setup).

steps.title: רב יהודה is hurt, and זוטרא keeps a one-day נזיפה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה stayed silent. When זוטרא asked again, רב יהודה answered sharply. זוטרא realized he had hurt him and kept a נזיפה on himself for one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה was silent and said nothing. זוטרא asked again: 'Last' means there were first ones, so what are they? רב יהודה said: 'What do you think, that someone who doesn't know the meaning of this פסוק is not a great man?' זוטרא realized רב יהודה was upset, and he kept a rebuke on himself for one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The story finishes, and it ends with a one-day נזיפה. This is the proof the גמרא wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's silence meant he did not know the answer. Asking again embarrassed him. זוטרא punished himself the way מר עוקבא did in Step 25, and again it was for exactly one day, which confirms the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, a great scholar
He took the matter to heart (was hurt)

steps.whatToRemember: All three stories (מר עוקבא, the woman, and זוטרא) end with a נזיפה of one day. That is the rule for בבל.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: He was silent and said nothing at all to him.
He asked him again: "Last"
implies that there are first ones.
What are the first ones?
He said to him: What do you think,
that someone who doesn't know the meaning of this verse
is not a great man?
He realized that he had taken the matter to heart,
so he kept a rebuke on himself for one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from Step 27 with the one-day נזיפה.
steps.raayaObject: A נזיפה in בבל lasts one day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זוטרא בר טוביה's self-imposed one-day נזיפה.

steps.title: So what are the 'first words' of דוד?
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic came up, the גמרא asks the question itself: what are the first words of דוד?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that we have come to this: 'last' implies there were first words. What are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of נזיפה for a moment to answer the question from the story. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from Step 27 was never answered in the story. The phrase 'now that we have come to it' signals a side question that the גמרא now resolves.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that we have come to it

phrases.english: And now that we have come to it,
anyway, "last"
implies that there are first ones.
What are the first ones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the question left unanswered in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words of דוד are the 'first words'?

steps.title: The first words are דוד's שירה
steps.stepSummary: The first words are the שירה that דוד sang when ה' saved him from all his enemies and from שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And דוד spoke to ה' the words of this song on the day ה' saved him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of שאול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the פסוק that opens the שירה one פרק earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פסוק calls the שירה 'words' (דברי השירה). So the שירה is the 'first words,' and the next פרק has the 'last words.'

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְדַבֵּר דָּוִד לַה׳ אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת
phrases.english: "And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song
on the day the Lord saved him
from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:1

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְדַבֵּר דָּוִד לַה׳ אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַשִּׁירָה הַזֹּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first words are the שירה of שמואל ב פרק כב, which the פסוק calls 'words.'

steps.title: ה׳ rebukes דוד for singing over שאול's downfall
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה says to דוד: you sing over the fall of שאול? If you were שאול and he were דוד, I would have given up many Davids for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב"ה said to דוד: דוד, you are singing a song about שאול's downfall? If you had been שאול and he had been דוד, I would have destroyed many like דוד for his sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a sharp point about the שירה from the last step: ה' was not pleased that דוד sang over שאול's fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said דוד's 'first words' were his song when he was saved from שאול. Now we learn that ה' rebuked him for it, because שאול as a person was greater than דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה')
If only / had it been that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even a fallen leader like שאול must be treated with respect, and celebrating his fall was a mistake even for דוד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to David:
David, are you saying a song
over the downfall of Saul?
If you had been Saul and he had been David
I would have destroyed many Davids before him.
phrases.notes: He means שאול was so great that, had their roles been switched, many Davids would have been given up for his sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds ה''s reaction to the שירה identified in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה' rebuked דוד for singing over שאול's fall, since שאול was greater than him.

steps.title: A פסוק about כוש בן ימיני hints to this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows this idea in a פסוק: 'שגיון לדוד אשר שר לה' על דברי כוש בן ימיני'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'A שגיון of דוד, which he sang to ה' about the words of כוש בן ימיני.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים that connects to the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'היינו דכתיב' means 'this is what the פסוק is talking about'. The word שגיון is commonly understood as hinting to a mistake, and 'כוש בן ימיני' points to שאול, who was from the tribe of בנימין. This sets up the next question about the name 'כוש'.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of song in תהלים, linked to the idea of error

phrases.english: This is what is written:
"A Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the Lord,
concerning the words of Cush the Benjaminite"
phrases.notes: תהלים 7:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק that reflects the rebuke of step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד's song over שאול is seen as a mistake

steps.title: Was שאול's name really כוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is his name כוש? His name is שאול!
steps.simpleTranslation: Is his name כוש? Isn't his name שאול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the פסוק: it calls שאול by the name 'כוש', which was not his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not really asking for information; it is pushing us to explain why the פסוק uses a strange name. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that...? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: But is Cush his name?
Isn't Saul his name!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כּוּשׁ שְׁמוֹ? וַהֲלֹא שָׁאוּל שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man was named שאול, so calling him כוש seems wrong.

steps.title: שאול stood out by his deeds like a כושי by his skin
steps.stepSummary: Just as a כושי stands out by his skin, שאול stood out by his good deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: just as a כושי stands out because of his skin, so too שאול stood out because of his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'כוש' is not a name but a description: שאול was different and special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person from כוש has skin that looks different from everyone around him. The פסוק uses this to say שאול's deeds were different from, and better than, other people's. This fits the rebuke of step 31 that שאול was truly great.

keyTerms.meaning: A person from כוש, a land in Africa

steps.confusionAlert: 'כושי' here is not an insult; it is praise, meaning the person stood out for good deeds.

phrases.english: Rather: just as a Cushite stands out in his skin
so too Saul stood out in his deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the word as a description instead of a name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כוש is a name, which does not fit שאול
steps.terutzMaskana: כוש describes how שאול stood out through his deeds

steps.title: The same reading for ציפורה, the כושית
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls משה's wife 'האשה הכושית', but her name was ציפורה; it means she stood out by her deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you can explain: 'about the כושית woman whom he had married.' Is her name כושית? Her name is ציפורה! Rather, just as a כושית stands out in her skin, so too ציפורה stood out in her deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same idea to explain another פסוק that uses the word 'כושית'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is exactly the same: a question (was that her name?) and the same answer (she stood out in her deeds). This shows the reading of 'כושי' is a general rule in the תנ"ך, not a one-time explanation.

phrases.english: Similarly, you can say:
"Because of the Cushite woman whom he had married"
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:1

phrases.english: But is Cushite her name?
Isn't Tzipporah her name!
Rather: just as a Cushite woman stands out in her skin
so too Tzipporah stood out in her deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading of step 34 to another פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כושי' in the תנ"ך means standing out in deeds

steps.title: The same reading for צדקיה, the כושי
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of 'עבד מלך הכושי', and the גמרא says this was צדקיה, who stood out by his deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you can explain: 'And עבד מלך הכושי heard.' Is his name כושי? His name is צדקיה! Rather, just as a כושי stands out in his skin, so too צדקיה stood out in his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same pattern a third time, to a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא identifies the man in the פסוק as צדקיה. Again, 'כושי' is read as praise for someone whose deeds stood out.

keyTerms.meaning: A man named in ירמיהו; literally 'servant of the king'
צדקיה, king of יהודה in the time of ירמיהו

phrases.english: Similarly, you can say:
"And Ebed-Melech the Cushite heard"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 38:7

phrases.english: But is Cushite his name?
Isn't Tzidkiyahu his name!
Rather: just as a Cushite stands out in his skin
so too Tzidkiyahu stood out in his deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another application of the same reading.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כושי' in the תנ"ך means standing out in deeds

steps.title: The same reading for the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares ישראל to 'בני כושיים'; it means ישראל stand out in their deeds from all the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you can explain: 'Are you not like the children of the כושיים to Me, בית ישראל?' Is their name כושיים? Their name is ישראל! Rather, just as a כושי stands out in his skin, so too ישראל stand out in their deeds from all the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same pattern one last time, now to the whole Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea grows from single people (שאול, ציפורה, צדקיה) to the entire nation. ישראל are 'different' from all other nations because of their deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of Israel, the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: Whenever the תנ"ך calls a special person or people 'כושי', the גמרא reads it as praise: just as a כושי stands out by his skin, they stand out by their deeds. This began with שאול, which is why דוד was wrong to sing over his fall.

phrases.english: Similarly, you can say:

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲלֹא כִבְנֵי כוּשִׁיִּים אַתֶּם לִי בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: "Are you not like the children of the Cushites to Me, house of Israel?"
phrases.notes: עמוס 9:7

phrases.english: But is Cushites their name?
Isn't Israel their name!
Rather: just as a Cushite stands out in his skin
so too Israel stand out in their deeds
from all the nations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final application of the same reading, now to the whole nation.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כושי' in the תנ"ך means standing out in deeds

steps.title: דוד raised up the yoke of repentance
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, reads 'הוקם על' as 'he raised up the yoke (עולה) of תשובה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the פסוק mean, 'The saying of דוד son of ישי, and the saying of the man raised up on high'? It means: the saying of דוד son of ישי, who raised up the yoke of תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the 'last words of דוד'. It reads one word in the פסוק in a new way to teach that דוד showed the world the power of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's word עָל ('on high') shares its letters with עוּלָּהּ ('yoke'). So instead of 'the man raised on high', the דרשה reads it as 'the man who raised up the yoke of תשובה'. דוד's own return to הקב"ה became a model for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: raised up on high (the plain meaning)
yoke, a load one takes upon oneself

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
What is meant by what is written:
"The saying of David son of Yishai,
and the saying of the man who was raised up on high"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:1

phrases.english: — The saying of David son of Yishai,
who raised up the yoke of repentance.
phrases.notes: עָל ('on high') and עוּלָּהּ ('yoke') share the same letters, so the גמרא reads the word as 'yoke'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the כושי דרשות to a new group of דרשות on the last words of דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הוקם על' means דוד raised up the yoke of תשובה.

steps.title: What does the פסוק about 'ruling over man' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The God of ישראל said, the Rock of ישראל spoke to me: ruler over man, a צדיק, ruling in the fear of God.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a hard פסוק and asks what it means. This sets up רבי אבהו's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the words are choppy: who rules, and who is the צדיק? The question 'מאי קאמר' shows the plain reading is unclear and needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rock of ישראל, a name for הקב"ה

phrases.english: "The God of Israel said,
the Rock of Israel spoke to me:
ruler over man, a righteous one,
ruling in the fear of God."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:3

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the same passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the unclear phrase 'מושל באדם צדיק'.

steps.title: A צדיק can cancel God's decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains: הקב"ה rules over man, and the צדיק 'rules' over Him, because הקב"ה makes a decree and the צדיק cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, this is what it is saying: The God of ישראל said, the Rock of ישראל spoke to me: I rule over man, and who rules over Me? The צדיק. For I make a decree, and he cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by splitting the פסוק into a question and an answer: 'I rule over man; who rules over Me? A צדיק.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מושל באדם' are הקב"ה speaking about Himself, and 'צדיק מושל' is the surprising answer. It is not that the צדיק is greater than הקב"ה. It means הקב"ה lets a צדיק's prayer and merit cancel a harsh decree.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it is saying

steps.confusionAlert: 'Who rules over Me? A צדיק' does not mean the צדיק overpowers הקב"ה. The גמרא explains it right away: a צדיק can get a decree cancelled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
This is what it is saying:
The God of Israel said,
the Rock of Israel spoke to me:
I rule over man;
who rules over Me? A righteous person,
for I make a decree and he cancels it.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the צדיק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב"ה rules over man, and a צדיק 'rules' over הקב"ה by cancelling His decrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches how powerful a צדיק's prayer and merit are.

steps.title: What does the list of דוד's warriors mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק listing דוד's mighty men, starting with 'יושב בשבת', and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These are the names of the mighty men of דוד: יושב בשבת, etc.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another פסוק from the same passage and asks what it means. This sets up רבי אבהו's new reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plainly, this is a list of דוד's soldiers by name. The question hints that the names can also be read as descriptions of something deeper.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'sitting in the seat'; in the פסוק, a name

phrases.english: "These are the names of the mighty men
who belonged to David:
Yoshev Bashevet, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:8. In the plain reading this is the name of one of the warriors.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 39, now on a later פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the list of 'mighty men' really refers to.

steps.title: These are the names of דוד's own mighty deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads 'גבורים' as 'גבורות': the names describe דוד's great deeds, not other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said, this is what it is saying: These are the names of the mighty acts of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers: the list is really about דוד's own great deeds. Each 'name' describes something he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'the warriors דוד had', he reads 'the mighty acts of דוד'. So each name that follows becomes a lesson about דוד's character. The next step explains the first one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said: This is what it is saying:
And these are the names of the mighty acts of David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'names of the mighty men' are the names of דוד's mighty deeds.

steps.title: 'יושב בשבת': דוד sat on the ground
steps.stepSummary: The first 'name', יושב בשבת, teaches that in the ישיבה דוד sat on the ground, not on pillows and cushions.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'יושב בשבת': when he sat in the ישיבה, he did not sit on pillows and cushions, only on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first 'mighty act': how דוד sat when he was in the ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יושב בשבת' is read as 'sitting in the sitting', meaning his seat in the ישיבה. The great deed is his humility: a king and teacher who still sat on the ground like a student.

keyTerms.meaning: pillows and cushions, the seat of an important person

phrases.english: "Yoshev Bashevet"
— when he would sit in the study hall,
he would not sit
on pillows and cushions,
but rather on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אבהו's reading to the first 'name' in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'יושב בשבת' means דוד sat on the ground in the ישיבה, not on pillows.

steps.title: After his teacher died, דוד still refused the pillows
steps.stepSummary: While דוד's teacher עירא היאירי was alive, עירא taught from pillows. After he died, דוד taught while sitting on the ground and refused the חכמים' request that he sit on pillows.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as his teacher עירא היאירי was alive, עירא taught the חכמים sitting on pillows and cushions. When he died, דוד taught the חכמים and sat on the ground. They said to him: Let the master sit on pillows and cushions! He did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind 'יושב בשבת'. Even when דוד became the teacher, he would not take the teacher's honored seat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While his rebbe was alive, it made sense for דוד to sit lower. The new point is that after עירא died, דוד was now the one teaching, and he still sat on the ground. Even when the חכמים urged him, he refused, which shows true humility.

keyTerms.meaning: he passed away (literally, his soul rested)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'mighty men' of דוד are read as his mighty deeds. The first is his humility: even as the head teacher, he sat on the ground and refused the honored seat.

phrases.english: For as long as
his teacher Ira the Jairite was alive,
he would teach the Sages
phrases.notes: 'He' here is עירא, the teacher, not דוד.

phrases.english: while sitting on pillows and cushions.
When he passed away,
David would teach the Sages,
and he would sit on the ground.
They said to him:
Let the master sit on pillows and cushions!
He did not accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכֹל כַּמָּה דַּהֲוָה רַבֵּיהּ עִירָא הַיָּאִירִי קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story behind step 43 and shows how great דוד's humility was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even as the head teacher after עירא's death, דוד sat on the ground and refused the honored seat.

steps.title: תחכמוני: Be Like Me
steps.stepSummary: רב reads תחכמוני as 'תהא כמוני': because דוד humbled himself, הקב"ה made him 'like Him', so הקב"ה decrees and דוד can cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'תחכמוני': רב said that הקב"ה told דוד, 'Since you made yourself low, be like Me. I make a decree, and you can cancel it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the פסוק, תחכמוני, and רב explains it as a reward for דוד's humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to step 44: דוד sat on the ground instead of on pillows, and here he is rewarded for that humility. רב reads the word תחכמוני as if it said תהא כמוני, 'be like Me'. 'Like Me' means having power over decrees, the same idea רבי אבהו taught in step 40.

keyTerms.meaning: A name in the פסוק, read here as 'תְּהֵא כָּמוֹנִי' (be like Me)

phrases.english: "Tachkemoni": Rav said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Since you have made yourself low,
phrases.notes: This refers back to דוד sitting on the ground instead of on pillows.

phrases.english: be like Me.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: תַּחְכְּמוֹנִי sounds like תְּהֵא כָּמוֹנִי.

phrases.english: For I make a decree,
and you cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues interpreting the names in the פסוק as praises of דוד, tying his humility from step 44 to a reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because דוד humbled himself, הקב"ה gave him the power to cancel divine decrees.

steps.title: Head of the Three אבות
steps.stepSummary: ראש השלישים is read as 'head of the three אבות': הקב"ה tells דוד he will be head of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Chief of the officers' means: you will be the head of the three אבות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next phrase, ראש השלישים, as another honor given to דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שלישים normally means officers, but here it is read as connected to שלשה, 'three'. The three are understood as the three אבות, and דוד is called their head.

keyTerms.meaning: Chief of the officers, read here as head of the three
The three אבות: אברהם, יצחק, יעקב

phrases.english: "Chief of the officers":
you will be a head to the three Patriarchs.
phrases.notes: שָּׁלִישִׁים is being read as if it came from שְׁלֹשָׁה, 'three'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase in the same פסוק, read as another honor promised to דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד is given a head position with the three אבות.

steps.title: Soft as a Worm, Hard as a Tree
steps.stepSummary: עדינו העצני: when learning תורה, דוד made himself soft and humble like a worm; in war he made himself hard like a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'עדינו העצני': when דוד sat and learned תורה he made himself soft like a worm, and when he went out to war he made himself hard like a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the name עדינו העצני as describing two sides of דוד's personality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדינו is read like מעדן (making soft), and העצני is read like עץ (tree). The point is that דוד acted the way each situation needed: humble and gentle in learning, strong and tough in battle.

keyTerms.meaning: A name in the פסוק, read as 'soft' and 'tree-like'

phrases.english: "He was Adino the Eznite":
when he would sit and occupy himself with Torah,
he would make himself soft like a worm,
phrases.notes: עֲדִינוֹ is read as מְעַדֵּן, 'making soft'.

phrases.english: and when he would go out to war,
he would make himself hard like a tree.
phrases.notes: הָעֶצְנִי is read as coming from עֵץ, 'tree'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next name in the פסוק, read as a description of דוד's character.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד was humble in תורה and tough in war.

steps.title: Eight Hundred at Once, and a Sigh for Two Hundred
steps.stepSummary: דוד could kill eight hundred with one arrow, but he sighed over the missing two hundred, because the תורה promises 'one shall chase a thousand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Over eight hundred slain at one time': he would throw an arrow and kill eight hundred at once, and he would sigh over the two hundred, as it says, 'How could one chase a thousand?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the end of the פסוק, eight hundred killed at once, and adds that דוד was upset it was not a thousand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים speaks of one person chasing a thousand. דוד reached eight hundred, so he felt that two hundred were missing from the full promise. This sets up the question of why he fell short, which the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How could one chase a thousand': the full promised number

phrases.english: "Over eight hundred slain at one time."
For he would throw an arrow,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַפִּיל שְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת חָלָל בְּפַעַם אֶחָת,
phrases.english: and bring down eight hundred slain at one time,
and he would sigh over the two hundred,
phrases.notes: The two hundred missing to reach a full thousand.

phrases.english: as it is written: "How could one chase a thousand."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the פסוק and raises a hidden problem: why only eight hundred and not a thousand?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד killed eight hundred at once but grieved that he did not reach the full thousand.

steps.title: The בת קול: Because of אוריה
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול explains that the missing two hundred were because of דוד's sin with אוריה החתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Except only in the matter of אוריה החתי.'
steps.whatsHappening: A בת קול answers דוד's sigh from the last step: the reason he did not reach a full thousand was the sin with אוריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote comes from a פסוק that says דוד did what was right his whole life, except for the matter of אוריה. That one sin is why the תורה's promise was not fully completed through him. So even this great praise of דוד ends with a reminder of his one failing.

keyTerms.meaning: Uriah the Hittite, whose wife בת שבע was taken by דוד

steps.whatToRemember: The names in the פסוק of דוד's mighty men are read as praises of דוד: humble like a worm and so 'like הקב"ה', head with the אבות, mighty in war. Yet his strength fell short of the full promise because of the sin with אוריה.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"Except only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 15:5. The full פסוק says דוד did right all his days except for this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question from step 48 about the missing two hundred.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did דוד fall two hundred short of the promised thousand?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because of the sin in the matter of אוריה החתי.

steps.title: Three versions of who said the next teaching
steps.stepSummary: Before giving a new teaching, the גמרא lists who said it, in three possible versions: רבי תנחום from רבי יעקב בר אחא from רבי שמלאי; or רבי תנחום from רב הונא; or רב הונא by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום, son of רבי חייא, from the village of עכו, said in the name of רבי יעקב בר אחא, who said in the name of רבי שמלאי. Some say it was רבי תנחום in the name of רב הונא. And some say רב הונא said it by himself:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is only telling us who said the teaching that comes next, and it records three different versions of the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is finishing the stories about דוד and starting a new statement, which seems to bring it back to the laws of נידוי. Read the chain from the end: the first speaker said it, and others passed it on. The phrase ואמרי לה ('and some say') adds a different tradition about the chain, but the teaching itself stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: By himself. He said it on his own, with no one earlier in the chain.
A man from the village of Akko. This tells us where the speaker came from.

steps.confusionAlert: This line has no teaching in it yet. Don't look for a rule here. It only tells you who said the rule that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum, son of Rabbi Chiya, said
a man of the village of Akko,
that Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said
that Rabbi Simlai said.
And some say: Rabbi Tanchum said
that Rav Huna said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא לְחוֹדֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna said it by himself:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the דרשות about דוד (Steps 38-49) and starts a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No rule yet. This line only gives three versions of who said the teaching that comes next.
